title: The Critic preflight prints the complete admit request, so the coordinator never hand-builds or guesses its keys
goal: Candidate 20e, G20-69 (PO standing goal: remove time-wasters seen in greenfield transcripts). MEASURED in the Claude greenfield TabletApp_claude_070_3 (2026-11-08, about 3 minutes and 15 tool calls): after `critic-dispatch-preflight.mjs` printed `packet-ready`, the coordinator had to hand-build `scratch/session-critic-finalization-request.json` for `session-critic-finalizer.mjs admit` by reading the finalizer source. It met SCF-REQUEST (closed key set), then learned that projectId must be the SAFE_ID form (lower case) and packetId 32 hex characters, then CPP-REVIEW-ADMISSION ('exactly one matching target ... found 0') until taskId named the last slice's dispatch id; the preflight's optional `--task-id` admission check (N13) was not used because nothing pointed at it. Build, runner-neutral: (1) the `packet-ready` result gains one additive field `admitRequest`: the complete closed request object for `session-critic-finalizer.mjs admit` (current schema version), with `review` copied from `dispatch.reviewerInput` and the coordinator-only prior-Critic binding exactly as admit expects, `projectId` in the form admit accepts, a freshly generated `packetId` of the accepted shape, `taskId` taken from `--task-id` when given (and then already admission-checked) or from the one dispatch record the review admission would match when exactly one exists, and only the fields the caller genuinely owns (route, verdictPath, event, sessionId where it cannot be read) left as explicit, typed placeholders that admit refuses with a message naming them; plus `admitCommand` (argv) writing it to `scratch/session-critic-finalization-request.json`; (2) when no `--task-id` is given and the admission would match zero or several targets, the result names `--task-id` and the candidate ids instead of leaving it to admit; (3) the packet-ready result's own next-step text (the field the coordinator already reads after the preflight) tells it to write `admitRequest` verbatim, fill only the named placeholders, and run `admitCommand`; skills/critic-review/SKILL.md, agents/critic.md, roles/critic.md, templates/prompts/critic-review.md and harness/review-protocol.md are covered by the Critic preimage pin (scripts/codex-isolated-critic-protected-preimage.v1.json) and must NOT change. (4) G20-71 (PO tile decision 2026-11-08: the default Claude Critic route stays opus): when the selected Critic route resolves to an Opus model (lib/model-role-route-source.mjs, critic_normal is `frontier` for epic/feature), the packet-ready result also carries the Critic dispatch prompt lines MP-07 requires, generated by the preflight itself: a non-empty `Batch scope (MP-07):` line naming the reviewed range (base..candidate and the module or file count) and a rationale line naming critical architecture or security, in the exact shape lib/dispatch-policy.mjs (DISPATCH-OPUS-NO-BATCH-RATIONALE, ~lines 292-304) admits, so the coordinator's default-route Critic dispatch is never refused; a non-Opus route carries no such lines. Add a regression case that the generated lines pass the dispatch-policy check unchanged. The result stays read-only (no packet, no state). If any file you must change is covered by the Critic preimage pin, STOP and report which file and why (never re-pin it). Restate in place with a G20-69 comment any test that deep-equals the packet-ready result (QG-04: never weaken another assertion). Add regression cases: packet-ready carries an admitRequest that admit accepts after only the placeholders are filled; a zero or ambiguous admission target names --task-id; the packet-ready next-step text names admitRequest and admitCommand; the Critic preimage suite stays green unchanged. Developed and tested in the clone named in facts; delivered as the held patch specs/sprint-alfred-epic/evidence/held-patches/w277-c20e-critic-admit-request.patch.
